Nina Mills was next away, clocking 19:02 to bring the team in 9th, and a now constantly improving Jacqui Smiter enjoyed herself on the final leg, picking off two of the opposition with her 17:56 effort.

She was also a member of the Southern Women's 3 x 800m gold medal winning team in 1987, along with Jacqui Smiter and Jackie Stone. Jacinta has been Track Captain since 1986 when she saw the team finish 7th in their first season in the Southern Women's League Division 2, narrowly missing promotion direct to Division 1.
These were Alex Barber, Angela Patten, Julia Cockram and Jacqui Smiter, and our best on record has been broken in three out of the six league matches.

Angela Patten and Gail Richardson covered the throws between them leaving Jacqui Smiter to fill in all the gaps. The two "J's", Georgina and Angela finally managed to compete in both relays with about 10-15 minutes rest.

And so we stay where we are for another year. Jacqui Smiter has survived her first year as Joint Team Manager and we now set our sights on 1997.
These are available from Jacqui Smiter:

For now though, let's get back to 1997 and offer our congratulations to Team Managers Cynthia James and Jacqui Smiter. Our thanks also to all those behind the scenes who did so much to help and of course a big "Well Done" to every member of the team.
We are always used to seeing Team Manager Jacqui Smiter in action but the third meeting at St. Alban's saw Cynthia James also leading by example.

The jumps, too, gave us some good scores with Julia Cockram taking the senior high jump and pole vault, Jacqui Smiter taking the 'B' high jump and Sabrina Scott notching up yet another long jump victory.

Jacqui Smiter has had a short spell in hospital for a wrist operation. We hope that her recovery is swift and look forward to her teaming up with Cynthia James again this summer to capitalize on our promotion the the Women's Southern League Division Two.

Our women's Southern League team, managed by Jacqui Smiter and Cynthia James, have subject to confirmation achieved their aim of gaining promotion to Division 2; and Sarah Roberts (400m) became our first female T&F international for a good few years.

Even joint team manager Jacqui Smiter got in on the winning act by picking up top score in the pole vault but in the end it was the local club that prevailed.

Throw in a couple of runners who missed their proper start times – Steve Fowler went off at about 14:25 instead of 14:00 while James Skilbeck-Nelson set out much later than he should have done – and poor Jacqui Smiter's asthma attack in mid-race, and one can see that there was as much drama in the event as ever.

After a closely fought match at Tilford our women's cross country team showed their new Team Manager Jacqui Smiter that they have no intention in spending longer than is necessary in Division Two of the Surrey League.
Fifteenth in 1997, this time around they cut their overall time by 3 minutes to move up to 6th – "Just one place lower than the men's team" a gleeful Jacqui Smiter announced.
